items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But he taught us the whole process of determining why certain chords are called what they’re called.

ctx.x: These gentleman that were involved in touching young musicians, were they themselves working musicians? Were they schoolteachers? Who were they in the community?

They were schoolteachers, but they were also working musicians, because they played – I remember Mr. Brown played many different instruments, and I think Mr. Franzman was a saxophone player and a theory teacher. Somehow we had one class with him. I don’t know how I got into it. But he taught us the whole process of determining why certain chords are called what they’re called. In one day he taught us that, one class. After that I knew exactly, whenever I was going to construct a chord, how it was constructed and…
When you’re interacting with the Montgomery family, would it be all of the brothers, or just Buddy?
